clue.text: Masseuse to avoid a bath toy

parts.note: a masseuse is someone who rubs people, a rubber
to duck something is to dodge it

explanation.surface: A spa worker tries to steer clear of the bathtub plaything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Masseuse' looks like a person in the scene, but it is read literally as one who rubs.
explanation.definitionFit: The yellow rubber duck is the classic floating plaything children have in the tub.

clue.text: Fix member of Congress's appearance

parts.note: a Rep is a member of the House of Representatives
an air is a look or manner

explanation.surface: A lawmaker's image needs sorting out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fix' could seem to belong to the politician's image, but it stands alone as the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To repair something is to mend it, a plain synonym of fix as a verb.

clue.text: Offshoot of second-rate farm…

parts.note: B is the grade below A, so second class
a ranch is a large stock farm

explanation.surface: An outpost of a mediocre farming operation.
explanation.definitionFit: A branch is a limb growing off a tree trunk, or by extension an outlying division.

clue.text: …comes into play :-0

definitions.note: the clue shows one face; the answer names the class it belongs to, plural

indicators.note: playing with things moves them about freely, so these letters get rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Continuing from the previous clue, the farm enters the action, to an astonished face.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis only joins the surface to the clue above; the wordplay here is self-contained. The definition is a typed face, an example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Emoticons are faces built from keyboard characters, and :-0 is the surprised one.

clue.text: Braved getting up to get a drink

indicators.note: in a down clue, getting up means reading from the bottom upward

parts.note: to face danger is to brave it

explanation.surface: Someone summoned courage to rise and fetch a beverage.
explanation.definitionFit: Decaf is coffee with the caffeine removed, ordered as a cup of it.

clue.text: Leader of aristocracy goes after peasant, ever since the time of Christ

definitions.text: ever since the time of Christ
definitions.note: the clue gives an adverbial phrase; the answer is the noun naming that span of years

indicators.note: following something means being placed behind it in the sequence

parts.note: a commoner is a person without noble rank

indicators.note: the leader is whatever comes at the very front, so only an initial is kept

parts.note: the initial of the word

explanation.surface: A nobleman trails a peasant, as has been the order of things for two millennia.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pits noble against peasant, but the definition is about the calendar.
explanation.definitionFit: The Common Era is the secular label for the years counted from Christ's birth, replacing AD.

clue.text: Prepare soup for work

indicators.note: preparing a dish means working its ingredients into a new form

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cook gets the broth ready before the shift starts.
explanation.definitionFit: An opus is a composition or artistic creation, often a numbered piece by a composer.

clue.text: Vehicles in space bid exploded

indicators.note: an explosion scatters the pieces, which fall back in another order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A rocket bid blows up before any craft reach orbit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vehicles in space' suggests spacecraft, but the definition is only 'Vehicles'.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedicabs are pedal-powered rickshaws that carry passengers for hire.

clue.text: Upside-down cakes under pressure

indicators.note: in a down clue, upside-down means the letters run from the bottom to the top

parts.note: cakes are sweet courses

explanation.surface: Pineapple upside-down cakes baked against the clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upside-down cakes' is a real bake, which hides the indicator in plain sight.
explanation.definitionFit: Being stressed is feeling strain or tension, the state of someone working under pressure.

clue.text: Young animal's leg, in part

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the young of a cow, elephant or whale
second meaning: the fleshy back of the lower leg

explanation.walkthrough: The possessive makes it look like one animal's limb; it simply joins two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: One word names both a baby bovine and the muscle at the back of the shin.

clue.text: Philosopher retreats in total panic

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the letters are read in the opposite direction
the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

parts.note: a run of letters straddling the two words

explanation.surface: A thinker flees in utter terror.
explanation.walkthrough: Read tOTAL Panic backwards to find PLATO.
explanation.definitionFit: Plato was the ancient Greek thinker, pupil of Socrates and author of the Republic.

clue.text: President informed mechanic in crisis

indicators.note: something in crisis is thrown into disorder, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: The head of state was briefed about a car repairer in trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: The US Constitution makes the president head of the armed forces, a title used as a synonym for the office.

clue.text: See 11
Places to work off frozen sweets

parts.note: taken as written
ices are frozen desserts such as sorbets

explanation.surface: Somewhere to burn off the ice creams you ate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Places to work off' reads like somewhere to exercise, but the definition stops at 'work'.
explanation.definitionFit: Offices are the rooms or buildings where people do their jobs.

clue.text: Complains loudly about broken bracelet — it can give you a jump

definitions.text: it can give you a jump

parts.note: booing is loud vocal disapproval

indicators.note: a broken item is in pieces that can be put back in a different order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone moans about a snapped wristband that apparently made them leap.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'jump' here is a jump-start for a car with a flat battery, the American sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A booster cable is a jumper lead clamped between two car batteries to jump-start a dead engine.

clue.text: Superficially Kafkaesque man captivated by sales pitch for a stiletto

indicators.note: someone captivated is held captive inside something else

parts.note: a spiel is a glib persuasive patter

indicators.note: the surface of a word is its outside, so only its two end letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters
the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: A man in a nightmarish Kafka world is won over by a pitch for a dagger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stiletto' suggests the dagger, but here it is the shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: A spike heel is a tall, very thin heel on a woman's shoe, also called a stiletto.

clue.text: Narrow escape from one in the same area code?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a near miss with disaster

definitions.text: from one in the same area code?
definitions.meaning: second meaning, taken literally: a phone call from someone nearby

explanation.walkthrough: An area code is the dialling prefix for a region of a phone network, so a caller sharing yours is close by; the question mark flags this whimsical reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A close call is an idiom for an accident or danger only just avoided.

clue.text: Gradually put battery terminals into a quarter?

indicators.note: putting one thing into another places it inside

parts.note: in American slang a quarter dollar is two bits

indicators.note: terminals are the end points, so just the first and last letters are taken

parts.note: first and last letters

explanation.surface: Slowly inserting a battery's contacts into a coin slot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terminals' fits a battery so well that it hides the letter selection. A bit was an old 12½-cent unit, so 'two bits' is a quarter.
explanation.definitionFit: Bit by bit means a little at a time, slowly and in small steps.

clue.text: Go too far, messing up voter's record

indicators.note: to mess something up is to throw it into disorder

parts.note: the apostrophe is ignored
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: Tampering with an elector's file would cross the line.
explanation.definitionFit: To overstep is to exceed a limit, as in overstepping one's authority.

clue.text: Detective and troublemaker on opposite sides of Venice's borders

indicators.note: one piece flanks the other on both sides, wrapping around it

parts.note: an instigator stirs up trouble

indicators.note: a border is the edge, so only the outermost letters of the place name are kept

parts.note: first and last letters of the city name

explanation.surface: A sleuth and a rabble-rouser take up positions at either end of Venice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Detective and troublemaker' looks like a pair of people, but 'and' just joins definition to wordplay; the troublemaker is split open for the city's edges to sit inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An investigator is someone who looks into crimes, a straightforward synonym for a sleuth.

clue.text: Squirt runs into Olympic swimmer

indicators.note: running into something puts one piece inside the other

parts.note: Mark Spitz won seven golds at the 1972 Games
R is the abbreviation for runs in baseball and cricket scores

explanation.surface: A little kid dashes into a gold-medal swimmer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Squirt' looks like a small child in the surface but is the verb for a spray.
explanation.definitionFit: To spritz is to spray a fine jet of liquid, as with a water bottle.

clue.text: Mysterious rune in the 5, like much e-mail

indicators.note: something mysterious is obscure and jumbled, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
5-down names the era since Christ, whose years are traditionally written AD

explanation.surface: An occult symbol from our own era appears in an inbox.
explanation.walkthrough: 5-down is COMMON ERA; a year in it is labelled AD, Anno Domini.
explanation.definitionFit: Unread messages are ones never opened, which describes a large share of most inboxes.

clue.text: Outpouring of what might cause a drunken brawl?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a sustained torrent, as of questions or abuse

definitions.text: what might cause a drunken brawl?
definitions.meaning: second meaning, read as two words: anger flaring up in a pub, on the model of road rage

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as BAR RAGE: the fury of drinkers, modelled on road rage, is a fair cause of a fight. The question mark flags the invented phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrage is a heavy, continuous stream of something, like gunfire or complaints.

clue.text: Top primate, at times

parts.note: apes are primates
X is the multiplication sign

explanation.surface: The dominant monkey only sometimes holds that position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top primate' reads as the leader of a troop, but 'Top' is alone the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An apex is the highest point or peak of something.

clue.text: Bite fish after turning over to ignore the alarm

indicators.note: turning over flips the whole string so it reads backwards
the second word's letters come later in the sequence than the first's

parts.note: a nip is a small bite
eels are fish

explanation.surface: An angler's catch bites, then rolls over, while someone dozes through the alarm.
explanation.walkthrough: NIP followed by EELS, all reversed, gives SLEEP IN; 'turning over' also suits the picture of rolling over in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: To sleep in is to stay in bed past the usual waking time, disregarding the clock.

clue.text: Holiday tradition maintained by Sudanese dervish

indicators.note: something maintained by others is held within them

parts.note: a run straddling the two words

explanation.surface: A whirling Sufi from Sudan keeps up a festive custom.
explanation.walkthrough: sudaneSE DERvish holds the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Seder is the ritual meal held at the start of the Jewish festival of Passover.

clue.text: Please German with tear for a painful conclusion

parts.note: bitte is the German word for please
to rend is to tear apart

explanation.surface: A polite request in German, paired with weeping, ends a sad story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tear' tempts you towards crying, but it is the ripping verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The bitter end is the final, unhappy outcome of something seen through to the last.

clue.text: To their buddies, conceivably, Einstein and Newton are similar

indicators.note: this phrase tells us to use the casual nicknames friends might call these men

parts.note: Albert shortened as a friend would
Isaac shortened to a pal's nickname, as in Eisenhower's Ike

explanation.surface: Pals of two great physicists might say the pair were much the same.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conceivably' admits nobody really called Newton Ike; it is the sort of name a buddy might use.
explanation.definitionFit: Alike means resembling each other, an adjective used after a verb like 'are'.

clue.text: At heart, nasty person is kind

indicators.note: the heart is the inside, so the answer sits within the following words

parts.note: a run straddling the two words

explanation.surface: A mean individual is secretly good-hearted.
explanation.walkthrough: nasTY PErson holds the answer; 'kind' looks like an adjective for niceness but is the noun meaning sort.
explanation.definitionFit: A type is a category or sort, as in 'that kind of thing'.

clue.text: Added an S to a dull prize, shockingly

indicators.note: a shock jolts things out of their places, so the letters land in new positions

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles that an extra S was tacked onto a boring award.
explanation.walkthrough: The American spelling with Z is what the fodder supplies.
explanation.definitionFit: Making a noun plural in English usually means adding an S on the end, as with cat to cats.
